_comment: The algorithm registry · docs/SCORING.md §4, loaded via ALGORITHMS_PATH.
Two rules govern what may be added here, and both are enforced at startup
by contract::algorithms rather than by review:
1. `1 + Σ(authority, structural, temporal, completeness, topical)` may
not exceed 2.00. The fused pool's own relevance spans 2.56x median but
only 1.31x at its narrowest, so a wider prior can reorder the pool on
metadata alone -- authority without relevance, invariant 9.
2. An entry with no `fitted` block loads as experimental: reachable by
name, absent from the tool schema's enum. The agent is never OFFERED a
weight vector nobody measured.
! Only two entries here carry numbers, because only two have been measured.
The per-query-type set of SCORING.md §4 is not shipped as a pile of
plausible guesses; it arrives when fit_factors.py has run per type.
! An unknown key anywhere in this file kills the process at startup. That is
deliberate: a typo that silently does nothing is the same defect class as
`topical` shipping at 0.25 while the engine evaluated it against NULL.
An entry may declare `composition` instead of `factors`. That is the general
form: any variable, any bounded shape, any number of terms. `factors` stays
the default because every fitted weight here was measured against it, and
the engine reproduces it term for term as a composition.
! The combination rule is NOT declarable and is not meant to be.
`relevance x (1 + sum(w_i * f_i))` is what encodes 'factors rank, but only
after relevance'. Every transform returns [0,1] by construction, which is
the only reason `sum(w)` is a bound that can be checked at startup.
Variables are bare columns -- regulation_type, article, chapter, about,
body, body_len, year -- or `number:<key>` / `text:<key>` for an enrichment
value the engine has never heard of. ! A weight on a key no row supplies is
a startup REFUSAL, not a silent zero.

balanced.description: The general case. Ranks on text, then lets an instrument's authority and structure reorder within what retrieval found. Start here.

fitted.note: Refitted 2026-11-14 on the 1.7M id_reg_markdown corpus and 196 labelled cases (fit_pool.py over the pool the engine builds, mirror 196/196 identical): the shipped weights are within noise of the best of 300 configurations on the 166 training cases (MRR 0.444 vs 0.451), so they stand. Against `literal` they win 16 cases and lose 11, +2.6 points Recall@5, 95% CI [-2.6, +7.7]: not a significant gain. The relevance floor demotes rather than removes since this refit: Recall@5 one case lower (0.577 -> 0.571), the answer inside the top 50 for 85.2% of cases instead of 78.1%. Σw = 1.0, prior bound 2.00x.

literal.description: No metadata prior at all: the arms' own fused order, unmodified. For a question where the wording is the answer, or to see what the retrieval layer alone believes.

fitted.note: 2026-11-14, the engine's own fused pool with factors off, same 196 cases as `balanced`.

balanced_expanded.description: EXPERIMENTAL. `balanced`, plus sibling clauses of the regulations that ranked. For when the right law is clearly being found but the wrong clause of it is coming back.

balanced_composed._note: EXPERIMENTAL, and deliberately identical to `balanced`. It exists to prove the assembled form on the deployment rather than only in a unit test: same five terms, same weights, written out. `algorithm_scenarios.py` asserts it returns the same ranking as `balanced`, which is what says the composition layer changed nothing. ! No `fitted` block -- it inherits no measurement by looking alike, and an unfitted entry is never offered in the tool schema.
balanced_composed.description: EXPERIMENTAL. `balanced`, written out as an assembled composition. Same ranking; the worked example of declaring a scoring function.
